companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/(loss)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's disclosed 'Core Local Commerce' segment operating profit, which bundles food delivery + instant retail/Flash Purchase + in-store/hotel/travel; company does not break out food delivery or instant retail losses standalone
companies.latest_signal: On the Q2 2026 call CEO Wang Xing said 'irrational competition is not sustainable' and CFO Shaohui Chen framed the shift toward marketing/operational efficiency under regulatory guidance; sell-side (Seeking Alpha) flags this as a possible 'temporary truce' rather than a structural fix pending final SAMR rules.

companies.label: Alibaba

periods.src: Alibaba June Quarter 2025 results (cited in later release)

companies.latest_signal: On the Aug 2026 call CEO Eddie Wu said Taobao Instant Commerce 'substantially improved unit economics and reduced losses' with quick-commerce revenue +45% YoY; Sina Finance (2026-08-21) headlined '份额保持、减亏加速，淘宝闪购稳了' (share held, loss-reduction accelerating), citing sell-side estimates that per-order losses have roughly halved since Oct 2025 vs the Jul-Aug 2025 peak.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed 'New Businesses' segment operating loss, which houses JD Food Delivery/JD Takeaway plus Jingxi, Joybuy, JD Property and overseas investments
companies.latest_signal: Q2 2026 release states losses 'narrowed significantly year-on-year, primarily driven by continued loss reduction at JD Food Delivery,' with management citing improved operational efficiency and a move away from 'growth-at-all-costs'; but the trend is not monotonic — losses actually widened Q2→Q3 2025 before flattening and then narrowing from Q1 2026 onward.

war_summary: Combined platform subsidy spend peaked around RMB100bn in a single quarter (Jul-Sep 2025) before SAMR intervention — flagging the food-delivery price war as a top 'involutionary competition' case in Jan 2026, re-summoning all seven major platforms in Feb 2026, and releasing draft rules in June 2026 banning long-duration mass subsidies and forced merchant/rider cost-sharing — forced a pullback. By Q2 2026 all three show sequential loss narrowing, Meituan most dramatically (loss to profit), but sell-side coverage frames this as a regulator-forced 'temporary truce' rather than a structural resolution, with durability into Q3/Q4 2026 the open question. Alibaba's disclosure is the weakest of the three (no standalone instant-commerce loss line since its restructuring), so its narrowing signal is inferred from a blended segment EBITA rather than a clean isolate.
note: Alibaba figures rely on English-language filings/wires (Businesswire, Morningstar, Fool transcript) plus one Sina Finance citation; LatePost/36kr/Caixin/Jiemian/21jingji were not directly surfaced with citable URLs by the research pass — treat the Alibaba and qualitative war-summary framing as needing a Chinese-source cross-check before use in a note.
